title: Masaya
goal: Buy a hammock and get the price down
culture: Masaya hammocks are the good ones and everybody knows it, which is reflected in the first number you are given. The haggle has the same shape as the leather bag in El Centro, one letter different: una hamaca is feminine, so it is me la deja en.

beats.es: Adelante. Hamacas de Masaya, hechas a mano.
beats.good: ¿A cómo? one last time. It has worked on a mango, a bundle of firewood and now a hammock.

beats.es: Mil ochocientos, y es de las buenas.
beats.good: You have done this in the market. The uy in front is free and it does half the work for you.

beats.es: Es que lleva tres días de trabajo, mire el tejido.
beats.en: Would you let me have it for twelve hundred?
ok: me la deja en mil doscientos
beats.good: Me lo deja en, me la deja en — the lo or the la follows the thing, and a hamaca is feminine. Same move as the leather bag, one letter different.

beats.es: Mil cuatrocientos y es suya. Ya no gano nada.
beats.good: Me la llevo — I’ll take it. Say it, pay it, and do not reopen the price. You learned that from the man with the leather bags.
